AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The selection and the transform are faithful -- 3 cards (CardsVar(3), Astrolabe.cs:18 vs astrolabe.py:17), chosen from the deck's transformable cards, each replaced and then upgraded, on the Niche stream -- but the upgrade is applied unconditionally where C# skips non-upgradable cards.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): `CardCmd.Upgrade(cardModel)` (Astrolabe.cs:26) silently skips a card whose IsUpgradable is false; the sim's `run.transform_card(card).upgrade()` (astrolabe.py:23) always increments upgrade_level
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `CardCmd.upgrade(hooks, card)` exists (cmds.py) and is CardCmd.cs:265-290's per-card body: the verb sits inside `if (!IsEnding)` and skips any card whose `IsUpgradable` is false, i.e. `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel` (CardModel.cs:785-789). 35 of the 203 ported cards are at MaxUpgradeLevel 0 (18 Curse, 14 Status, 3 Quest), and C# THROWS if CurrentUpgradeLevel is ever set above MaxUpgradeLevel (CardModel.cs:773-776) -- so the bare `card.upgrade()` was producing a state the source treats as impossible, and one conformance compares against the save as an (id, upgrade_level) pair. astrolabe.py routes its transformed cards through it. The reachability this entry established stands and is now the test: a Curse is transformable, transforms into another Curse, and every Curse is level-0.  Pinned by test/test_procure_and_upgrade_verbs.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: CardCmd.Upgrade(IEnumerable<CardModel>, style) guards each card with `if (!card.IsUpgradable)` and skips it; IsUpgradable is `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel` (CardModel.cs:785-789) with MaxUpgradeLevel virtual and defaulting to 1 (line 781). Card.upgrade() in the sim (cards/base.py:146-147) is a bare `self.upgrade_level += 1` with no guard, and astrolabe.py:23 calls it directly rather than through anything that checks Card.is_upgradable (cards/base.py:168-170) -- unlike relic/bellows, which does check. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed): CURSES ARE TRANSFORMABLE. RunState.transformable_cards() returns removable_cards() (run.py:406-408) and a probe confirms a Clumsy in the deck is included; C#'s own filter (CardSelectCmd.cs:487, `c.Type != CardType.Quest && c.IsTransformable`) likewise admits curses. Transforming a curse rolls another curse (run.transform_card routes CURSE cards to CURSE_POOL), and an executed run rolled curse_of_the_bell, whose max_upgrade_level is 0 -- an executed census finds 35 such cards (every curse and every status) -- and the unconditional .upgrade() then left it at upgrade_level 1, where C# leaves it at 0. The divergence is observable outside cosmetics: conformance/runner.py:618 compares the live deck as `(c.id, c.upgrade_level)` pairs against the save, so a spuriously-upgraded curse is a deck-parity failure; conformance/combat_driver.py:34 renders the '+' suffix from the same field. Astrolabe itself is obtainable via the ported Darv shrine (events/darv.py).

guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the port now draws on the named stream. sts2_rl/relics/astrolabe.py:26-28 resolves `niche = run.rng_set.niche` and passes it as `run.transform_card(card, pick_rng=niche)`, which is CreateRandomCardForTransform(item, isInCombat: false, Rng.Niche) (Astrolabe.cs:25); the legacy RL path keeps the shared rng by convention. WAS: the call went to the legacy shared random.Random, so the stream was never advanced and every later draw off it read at the wrong position.

guards.what: N2: `prefs.MinSelect` auto-select when the deck has 3 or fewer transformable cards (CardSelectCmd.cs:493-496)
guards.rationale: C# skips the selector entirely and transforms all of them; the sim's run.select_cards(purpose, candidates, count) is documented as mirroring CardSelectCmd.FromDeck* and takes the same candidate list and count, so a short list yields the whole list on both sides. Recorded because the auto-select branch also changes whether a player-choice id is reserved, which is a replay-visible difference in the game -- but not one the sim's single-player selector can observe.
Both sides no-op on an empty candidate list -- the sim's for loop over an empty selection does nothing. Not reachable with a real deck; no verdict rests on that.
